title: Crying Tiger Beef
subtitle: grilled marinated sirloin with a punchy dipping sauce
excerpt: Thick-cut grilled sirloin with a fiery, tangy Thai dipping sauce. Serves two in about 25 minutes.
sourceNotes: A favourite Thai-Isan grilled beef dish. The name refers to the heat of the sauce being enough to make a tiger weep.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate the beef up to 8 hours ahead. Make the dipping sauce a day ahead and refrigerate.

glossaryTerms.definition: Fermented fish liquid. Used in both the marinade and the dipping sauce.
A sour paste made from tamarind fruit. It gives the dipping sauce its deep fruity acidity.
A well-flavoured, tender cut from the loin. It grills quickly and stays juicy when cooked to medium.
Toasted and ground dried red chilli. It gives the dipping sauce a sustained heat rather than the bright hit of fresh chilli.

content.text: Crying tiger beef serves 2 and takes about 27 minutes including resting. The
is marinated briefly, then grilled hard until charred outside and pink within. The dipping sauce uses
for a punchy, sour heat. Rest the beef before slicing.
Rest the beef for at least 5 minutes after grilling. Slicing too soon lets the juices run out onto the board and the meat turns dry.
Mix the soy sauce, fish sauce, and caster sugar in a shallow dish. Add the beef and turn to coat. Leave at room temperature for 10 to 15 minutes while the griddle heats.

Make the dipping sauce. Combine the fish sauce, {{tamarind-paste}}, {{palm-sugar}}, chilli flakes, and lime juice in a small bowl. Stir until the sugar dissolves. Taste. It should be fiery, sour, and salty with a touch of sweetness.
Heat a griddle pan over very high heat until smoking. Shake any excess marinade off the beef.
Grill the beef for 3 to 4 minutes per side for medium. An instant-read thermometer should read 57 to 60 C at the centre for medium.
Rest the beef on a board for 5 minutes. Slice thinly across the grain.
Arrange the sliced beef on a plate. Top with fresh coriander. Serve the dipping sauce alongside with jasmine rice.

items.cause: Sliced with the grain rather than across it
items.fix: Always slice beef across the grain for tenderness. Look for the direction the muscle fibres run, then cut perpendicular to them.
Add a pinch more palm sugar and an extra splash of fish sauce to balance.

items.cause: Griddle pan was not hot enough
items.fix: Preheat the griddle for at least 3 minutes over the highest heat before adding the beef.

content.text: Crying tiger comes from the Isan region of northeastern Thailand. It is one of the classic dishes of Thai-Isan cooking. The dish is built on the contrast between the charred, savoury beef and the sharp, hot dipping sauce. Isan cuisine tends toward bold, assertive flavours. The heat in the sauce here is not background warmth but a front-of-mouth hit that gives the dish its name. Served with sticky rice and a simple salad, it is one of the most satisfying quick dinners in Thai cooking.
